The most common win left on "EASY MONEY" is $2. The second biggest prize left is $10,000, and two of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Everything above about "EASY MONEY" comes from the Florida Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
5057.headline: What the prize table shows

5059.body:
"THE CASH WHEEL" can match another game on price and top prize and still pay out very differently. This game is a game that pays many small prizes and few large ones. Of its unclaimed prize money, about three-quarters is in wins under $500 and the rest is in bigger prizes. Neither kind is better, and each suits different players.

The table below shows the full count for "THE CASH WHEEL", with every prize level included.
5059.headline: The prize mix in this game

5060.body:
"FIND THE 7S" is in the last part of its run, with about a quarter of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, top prizes are going faster than tickets, which is not a good sign.

Today's free summary of "FIND THE 7S" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
5060.headline: Tickets sold so far

5063.body:
CA$H IN HAND's prizes make it a game built around small prizes that are won often. Of the prize money still unclaimed, most is in wins under $1,000. The prize counts change every day, but this design does not.

The numbers for "CA$H IN HAND" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
